messages:
incident-bot: PAGER [P1] - Memory pressure anomaly detected on inference fleet (kv-cache arena fragmentation). Elevated CUDA OOMs and 95th/99th latency spikes observed for /v1/generate in us-west-2. Paging: maria

maria: I'm on rotation. seeing steady KV arena growth over last 12m, continuous-batching queue depth growing too. chart: https://telemetry/redwood/kv/arena/growth (screenshot attached). Customer-facing errors ~6% across Prod.

ryan: I can join. quick triage: logs show repeated small allocations not being reclaimed, fragmentation pattern. sample error: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.24 GiB (GPU 0; 40.00 GiB total capacity; 35.10 GiB already allocated; 1.75 GiB free; 2.50 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  File ".../inference/runtime.py", line 412, in forward
    out = model.generate(...)
```

jordana: suspected culprit: allocator churn + large continuous batches causing KV cache to retain lots of segmented slabs. we should mitigate live: 1) disable continuous batching for this model family 2) reduce max_batch_tokens 3) set TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF to encourage smaller splits.

tessa: Agree. I can flip routing config canary for the model group. Plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% if stable. Also will add env bump.

maria: Commands for quick action (canary):
```
# disable continuous batching for model-group
curl -X PATCH https://controlplane/api/routes/model-group-openbeta \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"continuous_batching": false, "max_batch_tokens": 512, "batch_timeout_ms": 12}'

# set allocator hint on hosts (systemd env example)
sudo systemctl set-environment TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF="max_split_size_mb:64"
sudo systemctl restart inference-agent --no-block
```

ops-bot: deploy started: canary route update -> 5% (jobs: deploy/route-update/3492).

tessa: canary applied on host pool canary-usw2-3. monitoring now.

ryan: on canary I'm already seeing reduced carbonation of small slab growth; KV memory curve flattens in the last 90s. good sign.

ops-bot: canary metrics: OOMs -> 0 on canary, p95 latency down 38% on canary. proceeding to 25%.

maria: rolling to 25% now. also pushing env change to Dedicated pools in usw2 (TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=max_split_size_mb:64). performing 2-phase roll to avoid cluster-wide spikes.

alex-cs: customer-impact update: Customer-42 reported 503s earlier, CS notified. please send ETA for fix so we can update them.

jordana: ETA: 30-45m for full rollout if no regressions. I'll prepare short incident note for customer comms.

ryan: additional mitigation: schedule an immediate arena compaction job to run on low-traffic nodes (experimental). command: 
```
# trigger manual compaction task
./tools/kv_compactor --pool=usw2-primary --mode=aggressive --dry-run=false
```

maria: running compaction on 2 nodes now. watching for transient latency impact.

ops-bot: compaction job started job-id=compaction-202471.

tessa: rolling to 100% routing now. will watch for 10m.

ryan: after 100% rollout: global OOM count dropped ~92% vs peak, error rate back down to baseline ~0.6%. KV arena graphs show plateau then slow decay.

maria: impact summary for timeline:
- 00:00 root alert (anomaly)
- +02m paging oncall
- +08m canary disable continuous batching
- +18m canary success -> progressive rollout
- +25m TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF env set on dedicated pools
- +35m manual arena compaction started
- +45m mitigation complete, customers restored

alex-cs: noted. customers updated. :thumbsup:

jordana: Post-incident next steps (assignments):
- run forensic memory traces on two affected hosts (ryan)
- confirm allocator/torch version regressions vs baseline (maria)
- evaluate default TORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF and whether to ship as permanent change (eng-runtime team) (jordana)
- write postmortem with impact numbers & action items (maria + alex-cs)

maria: marking P1 resolved for now. will keep this thread for postmortem drafts. assigning postmortem owner: maria.

incident-bot: Incident resolved and paged out. Severity: P1 -> Resolved. Postmortem owner: maria. Link: https://incidents/redwood/2472001234

ryan: a few follow-ups: test matrix to reproduce fragmentation with cont-batching + large context, check for model-specific allocation patterns. I'll start a perf experiment branch.

tessa: thanks all — excellent coordination. closing live mitigation.

maria: copying runbook notes into incident tracker and scheduling postmortem meeting for tomorrow 09:00 PT.
